note: Original simplified landscape compositions in a 100 × 56.25 coordinate space. Preserve aspect ratio: never normalise each skyline to a common summit height. Viewpoint is an editorial composition, not a surveyed camera position.

ben-nevis.viewpoint: North face from the Allt a’ Mhuilinn corrie
ben-nevis.features: Broad summit rim above deep gullies and buttresses.

ben-macdui.viewpoint: Across the Lairig Ghru from Cairn Toul
ben-macdui.features: A broad, gently domed plateau over a steep corrie wall.

cairn-gorm.features: Rounded summit dome set above wide northern corries.

schiehallion.viewpoint: Western end-on view from Loch Rannoch
schiehallion.features: Recognisable near-symmetrical cone; the long ridge is foreshortened from the west.

ben-lomond.features: A rounded summit above overlapping shoulders and the loch.

buachaille-etive-mor.viewpoint: Stob Dearg’s east face from Rannoch Moor
buachaille-etive-mor.features: A steep asymmetric pyramid with a broad rocky base.

bidean-nam-bian.viewpoint: Glen Coe looking into the Three Sisters and Lost Valley
bidean-nam-bian.features: Overlapping buttresses frame the valley; this shows the massif, not a falsely isolated summit.

meall-dearg.viewpoint: Along Aonach Eagach towards Meall Dearg
meall-dearg.features: A receding jagged crest with multiple notches, not a single pyramid.

liathach.features: A long terraced sandstone wall, broken by high summits and pinnacles.

an-teallach.viewpoint: Along the Corrag Bhuidhe pinnacles towards the wider An Teallach ridge
an-teallach.features: Stacked sandstone towers in the foreground, with an uneven skyline receding behind.

stac-pollaidh.features: A low elongated castellated crest on a broad grassy pedestal.

suilven.viewpoint: Broadside from the Glen Oykel approach
suilven.features: Two unequal summits separated by a pronounced saddle above low moorland.

ben-hope.features: A blunt summit with a steep western front and a long sloping shoulder.

sgurr-alasdair.viewpoint: From Coire Lagan towards the Great Stone Chute
sgurr-alasdair.features: Dark Cuillin walls and an unmistakably steep scree gully beneath the summit.

scafell-pike.features: Broken rock skyline and the adjoining crags enclosing Hollow Stones.

helvellyn.viewpoint: Facing the eastern headwall from Red Tarn
helvellyn.features: Broad summit rim between Striding and Swirral Edges, with Red Tarn below.

skiddaw.features: Several rounded, overlapping summits and substantial grassy shoulders.

blencathra.viewpoint: Looking along Sharp Edge above Scales Tarn
blencathra.features: A broad upper fell with a narrow rocky arête enclosing the tarn.

great-gable.viewpoint: From Wasdale Head towards Sty Head
great-gable.features: A bulky rocky dome with a steep shoulder and ribbed eastern face.

catbells.viewpoint: Across Derwentwater from the eastern shore
catbells.features: A compact rounded ridge, with a visible saddle between its tops.

haystacks.features: A low, lumpy craggy crest with numerous small tops.

fairfield.viewpoint: Along the southern horseshoe from Heron Pike
fairfield.features: Rounded successive ridges lead to a wide, nearly level summit.

bowfell.viewpoint: The Langdale face above the Three Tarns approach
bowfell.features: Angular summit above a long, uneven rocky shoulder.

pavey-ark.viewpoint: Facing the cliff from Stickle Tarn
pavey-ark.features: A broad wall with a gently arched rim and diagonal rock ledges.

kinder-scout.viewpoint: Southern plateau edge above Jacob’s Ladder
kinder-scout.features: A long low gritstone rim, with shallow undulations rather than a pointed top.

pen-y-ghent.features: A blunt stepped crown, distinct limestone bands and steep southern nose.

whernside.features: A gently rising, elongated whaleback with no pointed apex.

yr-wyddfa.viewpoint: Northern massif from the Llanberis side
yr-wyddfa.features: Yr Wyddfa rises behind long shoulders and neighbouring ridges.

tryfan.viewpoint: Northern profile from the Ogwen valley
tryfan.features: A steep fin of fractured rock with several summit teeth.

glyder-fawr.viewpoint: Cwm Idwal headwall and the Glyder plateau
glyder-fawr.features: A high broken plateau above steep slabs, rather than an isolated cone.

glyder-fach.viewpoint: Bristly Ridge approaching the shattered summit plateau
glyder-fach.features: Angular pinnacles and split rock towers on a high rocky shoulder.

cadair-idris.viewpoint: The southern corrie wall from Llyn Cau
cadair-idris.features: A broad bowl with a rocky central crown enclosing the lake.

pen-y-fan.viewpoint: Across the central Beacons from Cribyn
pen-y-fan.features: Wide flat summit cap, steep layered face and a long grassy shoulder.

cribyn.viewpoint: Facing Cribyn from Pen y Fan
cribyn.features: A sharper grassy wedge with a long receding ridge; distinct from Pen y Fan’s flat top.

y-garn.viewpoint: Eastern corrie from the shores of Llyn Idwal
y-garn.features: A broad rounded summit behind a steep corrie and rocky foreground ribs.

moel-siabod.viewpoint: Northeastern profile from the Capel Curig area
moel-siabod.features: An uneven rocky triangular crown over long grassy flanks.

pen-yr-ole-wen.viewpoint: Southern face across the Ogwen valley
pen-yr-ole-wen.features: A bulky pyramidal face rising above the lake, with long Carneddau shoulders.

fan-brycheiniog.viewpoint: Eastern escarpment above Llyn y Fan Fawr
fan-brycheiniog.features: A long near-level sandstone rim with a steep scalloped face above the lake.

slieve-donard.features: A broad rounded cone rising above wooded lower slopes.

slieve-binnian.viewpoint: Granite tors on the summit ridge
slieve-binnian.features: Stacked, rounded granite towers with deep horizontal joints.

zugspitze.viewpoint: Limestone walls above the Reintal and Zugspitzplatt
zugspitze.features: A high rocky headwall over a broad scree basin.

mulhacen.features: A broad gently sloping summit and a long high shoulder.

pico-ruivo.viewpoint: Rocky approach from Achada do Teixeira
pico-ruivo.features: Volcanic outcrops and vegetated shoulders along the approach.

mount-olympus.viewpoint: Mytikas and Skala from the high summit basin
mount-olympus.features: A blunt crenellated limestone crown beside the lower Skala shoulder.

mount-fuji.features: Sweeping concave volcanic flanks and a short flattened crater rim.

mount-kinabalu.viewpoint: Low’s Peak above the granite summit plateau
mount-kinabalu.features: A small pointed summit rising from an immense bare sloping granite platform.

mount-takao.features: A low rolling forest canopy, without a bare alpine summit.

mount-monadnock.features: A broad exposed rocky cap above a substantial forested base.

mount-washington.viewpoint: Western Presidential Range from Bretton Woods
mount-washington.features: A wide rounded summit with long shoulders and ravines.

half-dome.features: A near-vertical cut face meets the rounded granite dome.
